title: Cortical traveling wave analysis reveals weaker resting forward theta waves and greater task-related modulation in obsessive compulsive disorder.
summary: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is associated with abnormalities in large-scale brain network dynamics. Conventional electroencephalography (EEG) captures local oscillatory activity but does not characterize spatiotemporal propagation patterns. This study investigates cortical traveling waves, which index directional information flow across the cortex, to determine whether they provide novel insights into altered neural communication in OCD. Resting-state (eyes-closed) and task-based (Go/NoGo, Flanker) EEG were recorded from 25 individuals with OCD and 27 healthy controls (HCs). title: Quantification of peri-ictal magnetic resonance imaging abnormalities (PMA) in status epilepticus: Clinical and prognostic significance of PMA volume.
summary: Peri-ictal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities (PMA) are increasingly recognized in patients with status epilepticus (SE), but the clinical factors influencing their occurrence and extent remain incompletely understood. We aimed to quantify PMA and investigate the associations of PMA occurrence and volume with SE duration, etiology, and mortality. In this multicenter cohort study, comprising a retrospectively identified cohort and a prospectively recruited cohort, adult patients with SE who underwent brain MRI within 48 h of SE onset were included. title: Exploratory prediction of surgical outcomes in MRI-negative epilepsy using preoperative individualized morphometric networks.
summary: To explore whether preoperative individualized morphometric networks derived from structural MRI may provide discriminative information for predicting surgical outcomes in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-negative epilepsy. Thirty-one MRI-negative epilepsy patients who underwent epilepsy surgery were retrospectively included (17 seizure-free and 14 with seizure-recurrence) in this exploratory study. Individualized gray matter morphometric networks were constructed from preoperative T1-weighted MRI based on cortical thickness distribution features. title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Cytokine Expression and Relationships With Neurological Measures in Virologically Controlled People With HIV.
summary: Quantify cytokines in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of virologically suppressed people with HIV (PWH) and people without HIV (PWoH) and correlate these with neuroimaging, neuropsychometric (NP), and neurodegenerative measurements. CSF samples were collected from virologically suppressed PWH and demographically matched PWoH under a natural history protocol. Participants underwent annual lumbar puncture, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scans, and NP testing at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). title: Vascular Brain Injury in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
summary: Patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at higher risk of vascular brain lesions. Whether AF and HF synergistically amplify this risk is unclear. In this study, we explored the association of HF and AF and their interaction with the prevalence of MRI-detected vascular brain lesions. We analysed 2,712 participants from the Swiss-AF study who underwent standardized brain-MRI and categorised them based on their AF diagnosis and history of HF. In the brain-MRI, we assessed large non-cortical and cortical infarcts (LNCCI), small non-cortical infarcts (SNCI) and white matter hyperintensities (WMH). title: Manganese Deposition Encephalopathy Associated With Prolonged Total Parenteral Nutrition: A Case Report.
summary: Manganese encephalopathy is a rare neurological disorder most commonly associated with chronic occupational exposure or impaired hepatobiliary elimination. We report a case of suspected manganese deposition encephalopathy associated with prolonged total parenteral nutrition in a critically ill patient with severe abdominal disease and cholestatic dysfunction. A 50-year-old man was admitted with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, tachycardia, and jaundice. Computed tomography demonstrated acute pancreatitis with pancreatic necrosis, choledocholithiasis, cholelithiasis, and superior mesenteric artery thrombosis. title: Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension Presenting With Acute Orthostatic Headache: A Case Report.
summary: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) is an uncommon and frequently under-recognized cause of orthostatic headache, resulting from spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. We report the case of a 39-year-old woman who presented to the Manchester Royal Infirmary hospital with sudden-onset neck pain and headache associated with dizziness, vomiting, and presyncope, markedly worse on standing and relieved by lying flat. The patient's neurological examination was normal; however, she was hypotensive and unable to tolerate an upright posture. title: Paraparesis and left upper extremity weakness after total arch replacement with frozen elephant trunk: possible contributions of spinal cord ischaemia and cervical radiculopathy.
summary: An 82-year-old man underwent total arch replacement with the frozen elephant trunk technique for an aortic arch aneurysm. Upon awakening 3 hours postoperatively, the patient exhibited flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities and left upper extremity weakness, whereas the right upper extremity was largely preserved. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage and blood pressure augmentation were initiated for suspected spinal cord ischemia. Lower-extremity motor function partially recovered, but left upper-extremity weakness persisted. title: Attention selectively enhances collision sensitivity in the superficial SC, PBGN and centromedial amygdala to looming stimuli in the upper visual field.
summary: Accurate detection of impending collisions is essential for survival. While multiple subcortical pathways have been implicated in the detection of looming stimuli, the roles of top-down attention and conscious awareness in this process remain unclear. Using high-resolution fMRI, we investigated how top-down attention and conscious awareness influence subcortical processing of approaching objects on collision versus near-miss trajectories. title: The dual future of OPM-MEG: Clinical translation and naturalistic neuroscience.
summary: Optically pumped magnetometer magnetoencephalography (OPM-MEG) has moved beyond proof of principle. The decisive question is no longer whether cryogen-free sensors can detect neuromagnetic fields from the human brain with sufficient sensitivity, but whether complete systems can deliver clinical decision value and interpretable recordings during more naturalistic behaviour. Here we argue that OPM-MEG is developing along two partly overlapping trajectories. One is clinical translation, where usefulness depends more on reliable workflows, calibrated source localisation, auditable quality control, and empirical evidence for improved diagnostic or treatment decisions. title: Rapidly Progressive Alzheimer's Disease: Candidate Mechanisms and Diagnostic Challenges.
summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) usually follows a slowly progressive course, but some patients experience unusually rapid cognitive and functional decline. This clinical phenotype, commonly termed rapidly progressive Alzheimer's disease (rpAD), has no consensus definition; its status as a distinct biological entity remains unresolved, and its reported frequency depends strongly on operational criteria and referral settings. To synthesize current evidence, we conducted targeted literature searches (up to August 31, 2026) of clinical, neuropathological, and biomarker studies. title: Functional Recovery After Severe Postoperative Decline in Glioblastoma: The Importance of Reassessing Treatment Eligibility.
summary: Glioblastoma is the most common and aggressive primary malignant brain tumor in adults, and those arising in the frontal lobe can present with subtle cognitive and behavioral changes, often delaying diagnosis. We present a case of a 67-year-old male patient who presented with a two-week history of psychomotor slowing and progressive difficulty expressing himself, initially concerning for aphasia. Neurological examination suggested a frontal lobe syndrome rather than a true aphasic disorder. title: Cortical microinfarcts are associated with thalamic subregional volume and cognitive impairment in small vessel disease.
summary: Cortical cerebral microinfarcts (CMIs) are small but could induce tissue injury extending beyond the lesion core. The thalamus, as a central cortico-subcortical hub, may be particularly vulnerable to CMI-related remote injury, potentially linking focal cortical lesions to cognitive impairment in cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). We examined associations of CMI burden with thalamic atrophy and cognitive impairment in SVD patients. This cross-sectional study included 133 patients with SVD. title: Decoding Parkinson's disease: a systematic review of qEEG biomarkers across clinical domains.
summary: This systematic review synthesized evidence on quantitative EEG (qEEG) correlates of Parkinson's disease (PD) across five domains: cognition, motor function, pharmacological interventions, neuromodulation, and sleep/non-motor features, evaluating qEEG's potential as a biomarker across these clinical domains. Following PRISMA, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for studies published from 1991 to 2025. We included studies with ≥10 idiopathic PD patients, resting-state qEEG, and empirical data. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI checklists and AMSTAR. We included 89 studies. title: Patient-Informed Biomechanical Modeling Reveals Mechanical Mechanism of Brain Damage in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus.
summary: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a globally growing neurological disorder in older adults that is radiologically characterized by enlargement of ventricles. However, it remains unknown whether ventricular enlargement can produce biomechanical loading large enough to drive brain morphological changes and tissue damage. Here, we develop an anatomically detailed biomechanical model of aging human brain and apply ventricular enlargement using a three-dimensional displacement field derived from MRI of iNPH patients and age-matched controls. title: Cerebellar Topological Alterations Across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum.
summary: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized as a network disconnection syndrome. Despite evidence implicating the cerebellum in cognitive network integration, its associated electrophysiological network topology dynamics across the AD continuum remain unexplored. Methods: We enrolled 34 healthy controls (HC), 40 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 30 AD patients in this study. title: Differences in Near-Infrared Light Spectral Characteristics and Cranial MRI Parameters in Patients with Major Depressive Disorder.
summary: This study aimed to evaluate differences in cerebral hemodynamics and regional brain activity using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and resting-state functional MRI in patients with major depressive disorder compared with healthy controls. Sixty patients with major depressive disorder admitted to our hospital from June 2022 to June 2023 were selected as the major depressive disorder (MDD) group, and another 60 healthy controls with physical examination in our hospital during the same period were selected as the healthy control group. title: Blueberry Muffin Sign: A Diagnostic Histochemical Clue in Mitochondrial Myopathy.
summary: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO) is a rare manifestation of mitochondrial myopathy, marked by slowly progressive bilateral ptosis and ophthalmoplegia that can mimic other ocular myopathies, often leading to delayed diagnosis. We report a 63-year-old female with a 24-year history of slowly progressive bilateral ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, and proximal muscle weakness. title: Lithium Toxicity Following Initiation of Semaglutide in a Patient With Bipolar Disorder: A Case Report.
summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are increasingly prescribed for type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, including among patients with severe mental illness. Their effects on gastrointestinal motility, oral intake, and volume status raise concern for interactions with drugs with narrow therapeutic indices that are cleared almost entirely by the kidney, such as lithium. We describe a 69-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, stable for several years on lithium, who presented with acute confusion, dysarthria, and expressive aphasia. title: A Case of Treatment-Refractory Tumefactive Multiple Sclerosis Mimicking Brain Abscess.
summary: A 47-year-old female presented with one week of left facial numbness following recent dental extractions. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with and without contrast revealed a contrast-enhancing lesion in the right parieto-occipital lobe with mild diffusion restriction and surrounding vasogenic edema, as well as smaller enhancing lesions in the right frontal and parietal lobes. Empiric intravenous (IV) antibiotic treatment was started due to a high concern for odontogenic brain abscesses. title: Brain and Cardiometabolic Effects of Major Weight Loss in People With Obesity: Preliminary Cohort Findings.
summary: Given the overlap between obesity-related metabolic and vascular abnormalities and Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factors, it is critical to determine whether weight loss improves brain and cardiovascular health. This study examined whether ≥ 40% excess-weight loss is associated with improvements in cardiometabolic risk, brain structure, and cognition. The study was a longitudinal study of individuals with obesity undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery or medical/behavioral weight-loss treatment. title: Agreement and longitudinal repeatability of established brain volumetry pipelines across healthy controls, multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer's disease.
summary: Brain volume estimates are increasingly used as longitudinal endpoints in neuroimaging studies and clinical trials, but outputs from different segmentation pipelines may not be interchangeable. In this study, we performed a version-specific comparison of six established brain segmentation pipelines across healthy controls (HC; n = 20), people with multiple sclerosis (MS; n = 19), and people with Alzheimer's disease (AD; n = 50). FreeSurfer v6, FreeSurfer v7.2, SAMSEG, FastSurfer v1, SIENAX/SIENA-XL, and CAT12 were evaluated. title: Alterations in default mode network functional connectivity in semantic dementia.
summary: Progressive deterioration of semantic memory is a defining characteristic of the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia or semantic dementia (SD). Semantic deficits in SD are classically attributed to temporal lobe atrophy, in particular in the anterior temporal lobe. Recent neuroimaging studies have associated SD with disruptions of intrinsic connectivity networks during task and at rest, predominantly implicating regions of the semantic and language networks. title: Choroid plexus volume in metabolic syndrome: a cross-sectional neuroimaging study.
summary: Our investigation aimed to explore the associations between choroid plexus (CP) volume and metabolic syndrome (MetS) components and cognitive-motor performance in a cross-sectional sample. A total of 211 participants (73 with MetS and 138 non-MetS controls) were included in this study. CP volume was automatically segmented from 3D T1-weighted images using a 3D nnU-Net. CP volume was normalized to estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV) and expressed as the CP/eTIV ratio. title: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
summary: Functional movement disorder (FMD) is increasingly being recognized as a condition associated with abnormal brain network connectivity; however, effective treatment strategies remain limited. We report the case of a patient with severe FMD that developed following an occupational injury and was characterized by functional tremors accompanied by migraines and prominent autonomic symptoms. Based on electroencephalography (EEG) network analysis, low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area was administered, followed by staged rehabilitation incorporating visual feedback. title: Clinical and Epidemiological Profile of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy in a Colombian Referral Center: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
summary: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare 4-repeat tauopathy characterized by marked clinical heterogeneity and frequent diagnostic delay. Epidemiological and phenotypic data from Latin America remain limited. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of PSP in a Colombian referral center and to compare findings by sex and phenotype. We retrospectively reviewed PSP cases evaluated at a Colombian neurological referral center from 2013 to 2023. Demographic, clinical, neuroimaging, diagnostic, and treatment-related variables were extracted from medical records. title: A technical review of dynamic brain functional imaging combined with EEG spectral parameters in the screening of early-stage brain injury.
summary: Early-stage brain injury encompasses subtypes such as mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), silent stroke and subclinical brain injury. It is characterised by negative imaging findings, subtle symptoms and a high risk of long-term neurological deficits, presenting a key challenge in the early screening and prevention of neurological diseases. Traditional imaging techniques, such as structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT), can only identify organic morphological lesions. title: Neurodynamical heterogeneous spiking neural network for spatiotemporal cognitive signal processing.
summary: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) enable low-power brain-inspired computing via sparse binary spike transmission. Nevertheless, conventional homogeneous SNNs built exclusively upon leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons exhibit limited capacity for complex multi-scale temporal cognitive dynamics. Existing parametric-heterogeneous SNNs only tune internal hyperparameters within single-compartment LIF units and cannot capture diverse neuronal computations observed in biological circuits. Drawing inspiration from cross-neuronal dynamical heterogeneity in neural systems for multi-dimensional perception and cognition, this work proposes the Neurodynamical Heterogeneous Spiking Neural Network (NHSNN).

title: Red forehead dot syndrome: a case report and review of literature.
summary: Migraine is a common neurological disorder with a broad spectrum of sensory and autonomic manifestations. Visible, recurrent, localized cutaneous changes temporally associated with migraine attacks are rare. I report a 41-year-old Pakistani man with an approximately 21-year history of recurrent bilateral frontal and supra-orbital headaches associated with photophobia, phonophobia, and nausea. For many years, his attacks have been accompanied by recurrent, well-demarcated bilateral erythematous forehead changes in a distribution corresponding approximately to the ophthalmic (V1) trigeminal territory. title: Status Epilepticus in Children: Clinical Features, Management, and Outcomes in a Single-Center Experience.
summary: The classification of status epilepticus (SE) has undergone several revisions, with the most recent update published by the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) in 2015. However, in seizures lasting longer than 10 minutes, there is still no consensus on optimal drug selection. This retrospective study reviewed the medical records of patients diagnosed with SE and followed in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit, Pediatric Neurology, and Pediatric Emergency Unit at Erciyes University Faculty of Medicine. title: Fixel-wise Differences in White Matter Fiber-bundle Cross-section identified in Children who Stutter
summary: Developmental stuttering has been repeatedly linked to decreased white matter integrity and structural connectivity differences in major white matter tracts. Prior diffusion-weighted MRI studies reporting such white matter structural differences involved voxel-averaged tensor measures (e.g., fractional anisotropy (FA)). A well-acknowledged limitation of this approach, however, has been that it cannot resolve distinct fiber populations within crossing-fiber regions. title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with amyloid accumulation over 3 years in cognitively healthy adults
summary: Importance: Identifying potentially modifiable risk factors for Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a priority. The psychological debt hypothesis proposes that RNT may itself increase risk for AD. Objective: To determine whether RNT symptoms are associated with change in established neurobiological markers of AD risk over time.
